aspects.says: Delivery is at least once because a sender can't tell a lost message from a lost acknowledgement, and the repeat period couples sender and receiver.
basis: section:20.10. Design Note: Why Delivery Is at Least Once
aspects.reason: a design argument about why the protocol repeats; the receiver practice exercises its consequence

aspects.says: A queued reversal leaves only when the receiver answers it; a late approval does not withdraw it.
basis: section:20.2. An Entry Is Stored Before Anyone Is Told, and Leaves Only When It Is Acknowledged

aspects.says: One sender per link takes only the head, so entries about one transaction reach the receiver in the order they were decided.
basis: section:20.5. One Sender per Link Delivers Entries in the Order They Were Decided

aspects.says: At the network's limit, in attempts or time from the first attempt, an entry is parked in its stored form and reported, and the next entry goes.
basis: section:20.4. After the Network's Limit an Entry Is Parked and Reported, Never Deleted

aspects.says: The receiver identifies a message by what its repeats share, posts it once, applies a reversal once, and remembers a reversal that found nothing so its late original is never posted.
basis: section:20.6. The Receiver Applies Each Advice Once, by an Identity Its Repeats Share

aspects.says: Later attempts are repeats; the wait doubles from a base up to a cap, and a reconnect makes the head due at once without resetting its count.
basis: section:20.3. Every Later Attempt Is a Repeat, and the Wait Grows Until a Reconnect Cuts It Short

aspects.says: A SAF stores advices (0120, 0220, 0420) in their first form, never a request, a response or a repeat, and nothing that proves the card; a request that can't be sent fails at once.
basis: section:20.1. A SAF Holds Reports of Decisions Already Taken, Never a Request

aspects.says: The reversal is stored, in the same transaction as its journal record, before the terminal is told the purchase failed.
basis: section:20.2. An Entry Is Stored Before Anyone Is Told, and Leaves Only When It Is Acknowledged
